borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions:
<div><span style="font-size:11pt">The proposed development, by reason of scale, siting, design, bulk, mass and appearance would be an&nbsp; undesirable &nbsp;addition,&nbsp;representing an uncharacteristic addition to the dwelling. The side extension would sit uncomfortably to the side of the host dwelling, significantly impacting the symmetry of the terrace dwelling, and failing to be appropriately designed, with an overhang proposed at the first floor level. The side extension would be significantly visible from public vantage points and would be visually intrusive, represent poor design and would be out of character in the context of the area. <span style="margin-bottom:0px; margin-left:20px; margin-right:20px; margin-top:0px"><span style="text-align:justify">The application proposes a first floor side extension that overhangs at the first floor level, with the provided plans being inconsistent in terms of design, setback and layout.&nbsp; </span></span>As such, the proposal would cause undue harm to the character and appearance of the host dwelling and surrounding area, including to the historic distinctiveness of the Becontree Estate. The proposal is therefore contrary to the following policies which seek to ensure that development recognises local character and promotes good design whilst protecting and enhancing historic environments:</span></div><div><br></div><div><p><span style="font-size: 10.5pt; font-family: " pt="" sans",="" sans-serif;"="">-
National Planning Policy Framework </span>National Planning Policy Framework
